svg.title: GLM-5.3's safety hold, itemized: top open score above, a coordinated-disclosure ledger below, both on a five-day timer to open weights
svg.desc: A split diagram organised around a horizontal timeline. The timeline runs from August 14, when GLM-5.3 launched with its weights held, through today, August 23, to about August 28, the promised open-weights drop, now roughly five days away. Above the timeline sits the reason to want the model open: it scores Intelligence Index 60 on Artificial Analysis, tying Kimi K3 as the top open model and landing just 3 points below the frozen closed ceiling of Claude Opus 5 at 63, and the plus-7 jump over GLM-5.2 came from post-training alone on the same 743-billion-parameter base. A dashed amber band across the very top marks that closed ceiling, frozen for a seventh straight brief with no Index-64 model and no flagship price cut since July 24. Below the timeline sits the reason the weights are held: a public coordinated-vulnerability-disclosure ledger at cvd.z.ai recording 2,436 vulnerabilities across 269 open-source projects after review and deduplication, of which 1,097 are critical in Linux, WebKit and FreeBSD; 53 CVEs are already assigned while 2,383 remain under embargo; the oldest flaw dates to 1981 and the mean time the bugs sat undiscovered is 26.6 years. A central caption states the tension: the same post-training that rebuilt the coding ladder also produced emergent exploit-chain capability, so the best open score on the board is also a prolific real-world vulnerability finder, and that dual-use capability is exactly what a weight release cannot be taken back.
svg.text: GLM-5.3: the safety hold, itemized
Top open score on the board — held behind a public vulnerability-disclosure ledger, ~5 days from an open-weights drop
CLOSED CEILING — frozen 7th brief:
Opus 5 63 (#1, uncut $5/$25) · Fable 5 62.1 · Grok 4.6 60.9 · no Index-64 · no flagship cut since Jul 24
▲ Why you want it open — capability
Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (v4.1.1, max): 60 — ties Kimi K3 as the top OPEN model, just 3 below Opus 5 (63)
+7 over GLM-5.2 (53) from POST-TRAINING alone — same 743B MoE base, ~40B active · ~93 tok/s vs Kimi K3's ~41 (743B vs 2.8T)
Aggregate Index is third-party measured; component coding/cyber benches remain vendor-reported.
Aug 14
launch — weights HELD
Aug 23 · TODAY
ledger public · timer holds
~Aug 28
promised open-weights drop?
▼ Why it's held — a public coordinated-disclosure ledger (cvd.z.ai)
2,436 vulnerabilities across 269 open-source projects (after expert review + dedup) — 1,097 critical in Linux, WebKit, FreeBSD
53 CVEs assigned so far · 2,383 under embargo in coordinated disclosure — e.g. Linux 6lowpan UAF, WebKit memory, FreeBSD ptrace, GStreamer, Suricata, Joomla
Oldest flaw dates to 1981 · mean latency 26.6 years undiscovered · ExploitBench 54.4%, 105 ExploitGym tasks in 2 hrs (vendor-reported)
Z.ai says its "most extensive risk review to date" hardens the model before release — the concrete content of the ~Aug-28 hold.
The dual-use crux, made concrete:
the same post-training pass that rebuilt the coding ladder (+7) also produced emergent exploit-chain capability.
Takeaway: the best OPEN score on the board is also a prolific real-world vulnerability finder —
and that capability is exactly what a weight release can't take back. The frontier is still approached from below;
this window the story is not a new number but the itemized reason the top open model ships on a timer rather than a link.
